title: Prometheus push/pull hybrid adapter with LLM KPI virtualization
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a lightweight hybrid adapter that accepts both Prometheus-style pushes from edge and dedicated nodes and exposes a Prometheus pull endpoint for central scraping. The adapter will also perform KPI virtualization for LLM-specific signals (token_count, kv_cache_hit, prompt_bucket, per_route_latency_histogram) so downstream dashboards and SLOs can be driven from a consistent canonical schema without exploding label cardinality across tenants and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts Prometheus pushgateway-style metrics and OTLP/Prometheus remote_write both, converting into a canonical internal envelope for downstream consumers.

Exposes a stable /metrics pull endpoint that supports Prometheus scrape and returns synthesized virtualized metrics for: token_count (per-route, model_family), kv_cache_hit_rate (moving-window), prompt_length_buckets, and per_route_latency_histogram with exemplars linked to trace ids.

Supports per-tenant label rewrite rules and cardinality caps configured via the control plane; when caps are hit adapter emits a telemetry counter and applies deterministic bucketing rather than dropping metrics silently.
Backpressure + buffering strategy prevents overloaded downstream remote_write backends from dropping incoming pushes; adapter exposes health and queue-length stats for autoscaling.
Works in zone-aware mode: edge instances can forward to local aggregator and fall back to regional endpoints when network is unstable.
Integration tests that validate exemplar-trace linkage, histogram stability under high QPS, and label-canonicalization logic pass in CI (integration suite).
Performance target: adapter additional p99 latency under 2ms for passthrough and <30ms for heavy virtualization paths at 2000 rps per instance on c5.4xlarge equivalent.
Documentation and runbook updated: config examples, failure modes, scaling guidance, and migration path from existing Prometheus pushgateway ingestion.
implementation_steps: Prototype ingestion pipeline: accept prometheus push and otlp metrics -> normalize to internal metric envelope (step 1).
Add label-canonicalizer and per-tenant config: deterministic bucketing and label rewrite rules (step 2).
Implement LLM KPI virtualization module: derive token_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, prompt_length_buckets and per_route_latency_histogram from incoming telemetry and enriched trace context (step 3).
Expose /metrics scrape endpoint with synthesized metrics and exemplars; ensure prometheus export format compatibility (step 4).
Add backpressure queue and persistent buffer with configurable retention and circuit-breaker to remote_write sinks (step 5).
Create integration tests and load tests that simulate dedicated nodes and edge push patterns (step 6).
Rollout plan: canary in observability-us-west followed by staged regional rollout and migration docs (step 7).
config_examples:
# example: per-tenant config snippet
tenant: acme-corp
label_rewrites:
  - from: 'instance'
    to: 'node_id'
cardinality_cap: 200
virtual_metrics:
  - name: 'token_count'
    derived_from: ['tokens_generated_total']
  - name: 'kv_cache_hit_rate'
    derived_from: ['kv_hits_total','kv_lookups_total']

# otlp example (pseudo)
ot collector: endpoint=http://adapter.local:55680 proto=otlp
# scrape target example
- job_name: 'adapter-scrape'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['adapter.local:9100']
tradeoffs_and_risks: Virtualization reduces cardinality for downstream storage but creates potential mismatch between raw payloads and synthesized metrics — we must provide raw viewport access for debugging.

Adding exemplar linkage requires stable trace sampling IDs from request paths; if sampling is aggressive we lose trace context for tails — mitigated by deterministic exemplar promotion for high-error latency buckets.
Backpressure buffer increases durability but raises disk and memory footprint on adapter; we will make retention configurable and rely on autoscaling for peak windows.
Label rewrite rules introduce potential for misconfiguration causing over-aggregation — add linting and dry-run mode in control plane to preview changes.
Running adapter in edge zones increases operational surface area (upgrades, config drift); we will provide a lightweight autoupdater and health checks to reduce drift.
Security: adapter terminates incoming telemetry connections; must go through security review for TLS, auth, and tenant isolation.
